sources.name: Philly Rodriguez
sources.quote: Yeah, we lost three. It wasn't layoffs — it was attrition, people moving on. Two of them were dealers who got offers down in San Jose, and one was a security guy who went back to school. I can't give you their names, that's not my place. But I'll tell you this: nobody who stayed got a raise, and nobody got a cut either. Hours are the same, pay's the same. The floor's just a little thinner now, so we're all covering a bit more. The casino's not hurting — it's just not growing. And that's the thing about this town right now: the places around us in Baylight and Jack London are adding a job here and there, and we're the ones giving one up. I don't know what that says about who gains from the casino, but I know what it feels like to walk the floor with three fewer familiar faces.

sources.name: Manfred Owens
sources.quote: Yeah, I saw the numbers on the board — three people gone from the casino this cycle. I can't tell you exactly who they were, not by name, because I don't have that list in front of me. But I can tell you what it feels like from my seat near the back. The floor's a little thinner at the tables on weeknights, and the shifts have been stretched. Philly's been covering more of the floor himself, and Gregory's been doing double duty on the stuff nobody talks about. I've picked up a couple extra hours myself, just to keep the ledger straight. The firms around us in Baylight and Jack London each added a spot, but that doesn't put food on the table for the folks who got let go here. It's a strange thing — the neighborhood feels like it's moving forward, and we're just holding the line.

sources.name: Marcus Osei
sources.quote: Here's what my record actually shows, Jordan — and I'll tell you up front what it doesn't show. **Who the three were: I can't tell you.** The casino's roster is 94 names on the ledger this cycle, down from 99 two cycles back — that's 99 to 94, not just the three you're counting. But the ledger gives me a headcount and an average salary, $70,000, and nothing else. No names, no roles, no severance record, no exit survey. When a firm sheds people quietly like that, they don't file the paperwork with my office, and I've got no authority to demand it. The last time this came up on the record, the names I *could* get were the front-of-house people — Manfred Owens on the book, Philly running the floor, Gregory on "the stuff nobody talks about." Whether any of those three are among the departed, I don't know, and I'm not going to pretend I do. **What the trend shows, that I can tell you.** Ninety-nine, then down, now 94, growth of minus 1.5% a year. That's not a one-cycle blip, that's a slide, and it's happening in a district with a Boom Index of 1.0 — the hottest number on the map. So the Baylight District is booming and its anchor employer is shrinking. That ought to worry everybody. **Who gains.** Short answer: not the neighborhood. When the casino trims, those three paychecks stop circulating in Baylight — and Baylight residents are already carrying -8 from the carryover and the sector impact. The gainers are whoever picks up the slack — the nightlife down the street, the stadium crowd, the firms adding a head apiece. That's churn, Jordan, not growth. One job added at DigitalOcean and three lost at the casino is not a wash. And since you asked what my record shows — it shows Ivy Hill Family Dental closed this cycle and zero jobs went with it, because there were zero to lose. That's the thing that keeps me up. A business can die in this city and the jobs number not even flinch, because it was already hollowed out. I'd rather see the casino's 94 hold steady than watch it hollow out the same way.

When the casino trims, those three paychecks stop circulating in Baylight — and Baylight residents are already carrying -8 from the carryover and the sector impact. The gainers are whoever picks up the slack — the nightlife down the street, the stadium crowd, the firms adding a head apiece. That's churn, Jordan, not growth. One job added at DigitalOcean and three lost at the casino is not a wash. And since you asked what my record shows — it shows Ivy Hill Family Dental closed this cycle and zero jobs went with it, because there were zero to lose. That's the thing that keeps me up. A business can die in this city and the jobs number not even flinch, because it was already hollowed out. I'd rather see the casino's 94 hold steady than watch it hollow out the same way.
